Our School Values Community | Respect | Engagement | Aspiration | Trust | Equality
Making A Difference Where It Really Matters

Specialist Subjects
Drama
At Phoenix we believe in the importance of Drama for our pupils, and the multifaceted benefits it holds for the development of their social skills, self-esteem, communication, and confidence. The Drama curriculum is designed to allow children to respond to a range of multi-sensory stimuli through a variety of activities which aim to engage and challenge.
Pupils attend weekly lessons with their class, which are delivered by a Drama specialist, using approaches which are grounded in movement, song, and play. Lessons build upon a repertoire of skills; ranging from engaging with props, initiating and enjoying role play to using emotion and performing in character. Drama and the arts are an essential part of school life at Phoenix and there are multiple performance opportunities, unique events, and special assemblies throughout the academic year.
Music
At Phoenix we believe that every child can achieve musical goals and find benefits in music. We provide specialist led, high-quality music education throughout our pupils’ school career and offer many opportunities to perform and work with creative partners in our local community. Our curriculum is grounded in the Sounds of Intent framework of musical development (SOI) which outlines musical development according to the interactive (making music with others), proactive (making music alone) and reactive (listening and responding to music) and it is specifically designed to support the musical attainment of children with special needs. Music lessons are therefore designed to be interactive, prioritising the use of live music making, music technology, singing, improvisation, dance and movement and many opportunities for self-expression.
PE
At Phoenix, we prioritise Physical Education as an integral component of our pupils’ confidence and well-being. Our PE curriculum is designed to equip them with skills that enhance their school experience and promote lifelong engagement in leisure activities. By fostering a safe and supportive environment, physical education plays a crucial role in shaping our pupils’ physical and emotional development, contributing to their overall health and instilling positive habits for a successful future.
Horticulture
Our Horticulture curriculum aims to support pupils’ holistic development through gardening, nature based and forest school activities. Pupils are encouraged to connect with and enjoy nature as well as developing practical gardening skills. Lessons are determined by the natural cycle of the seasons and take place outdoors as far as possible. We make links to real life, for instance tasting and cooking food we have grown from seed and weekly work experience sessions in Victoria Park. As pupils progress through the school, they experience growing and selling plants through our on-site Garden Centre.
Secondary DT
Through our Design and Technology Curriculum, we aim to develop pupil independence and communication skills through focused practical tasks that relate to the world around them. Through exploration, investigation, design, adaptation and reflection , pupils expand their knowledge of tools, materials, and processes. The DT provision is also integral in the understanding and awareness of global, environmental and sustainability issues.
Secondary ART
At Phoenix Upper, our dedicated art teacher guides pupils through the secondary art curriculum, offering a blend of two- and three-dimensional artistic processes in practical lessons. With a focus on skill development, knowledge acquisition, and a deeper understanding of the art realm, our pupils immerse themselves in both visual exploration and the sensory joys of artistic expression. Encouraged to reflect, experiment, and embrace flexibility in their creative approach, pupils showcase their artwork to the broader school community. Art at Phoenix is more than just a subject—it serves as a vital conduit for self-expression, bolstering self-esteem, and honing communication skills.
Secondary FOOD TECHNOLOGY
Through our Food Technology Curriculum, we aim to develop pupils’ knowledge and understanding of Ingredients, equipment and processes. Our students follow visual recipes to create healthy meals that could easily be recreated at home. During practical tasks Students build on their awareness of hygiene and food safety, they are also encouraged to adapt recipes to suit different diets and tastes. We design our units of work to ensure pupils have access to food and recipes from around the globe, that are suitable for different occasions.
Primary Interventions
The Intervention Leads at Primary Primary foster an enjoyable and dynamic learning environment where pupils can thrive through playful engagement. We employ a diverse array of activities that not only make learning enjoyable but also actively contribute to the development of both fine and gross motor skills. Beyond the physical aspect, we aspire to cultivate positive relationships with food by introducing a variety of textures and flavors. This approach empowers children to explore the world of nutrition at their own pace, nurturing a healthy and balanced perspective towards food while promoting overall well-being.
Primary Sensory Room
In the Primary Sensory room, thematic termly topics, social stories, multinational festivals, holidays, and sensory stories are explored using a variety of resources and approaches. This enables explorer, discover, and pioneer pupils to access, engage, and understand diverse themes and topics. Since learning occurs through play, the sessions are designed to be experiential, explorative, fun, and engaging. We integrate elements of Math, English, Communication, and PSHE into our sessions, creating activities and experiences that pupils both enjoy and understand, leaving them feeling enriched. Throughout these sessions, specific intensive interactive strategies are implemented to assist pupils in accessing not only the covered topics but also the communication engagement models used at Phoenix.
School Libraries
Our school Librarians at the Primary and Upper sites run sessions with all classes where a range of texts are made accessible, fun and engaging. The aim of the library space is to help our pupils better engage with books from independent choice making through storytelling, re-enacting and choosing props for role play.

PSHE / RSE
At Phoenix we believe that Personal, Social, Health and Economic (PSHE) Education and Relationship and Sex Education (RSE) are important aspects of the curriculum. PSHE and RSE have a dedicated lead at both the Primary and Secondary site.Both subjects support children and young people to learn about themselves and helps them to make informed decisions about their lives for example with their own health, relationships and online safety. The PSHE/RSE curriculum is tailored to meet the needs of the students across the different pathways and differentiated to ensure content is meaningful and applicable to our young people’s lives.

About Outreach
WHO ARE WE?
The Phoenix Outreach Service (POS) consists of eight specialist advisory teachers with experience and expertise in supporting autistic pupils.
WHAT DO WE DO?
Our vision as a service is to provide effective support for autistic pupils in mainstream schools across the borough of Tower Hamlets. We see Phoenix as a centre of excellence for supporting autistic pupils of all ages. Through the Phoenix Outreach Service, we aim to share this excellent practice with mainstream schools to support successful inclusion in their school settings.
We work with autistic pupils from the age of 3 to 19 in mainstream, maintained school settings. We provide training for key staff, and for organisations within the community. We run termly parents’ evenings and a programme of parent workshops and courses throughout the year, hosted by mainstream schools.
WHO DO WE SUPPORT?
Each outreach teacher works with a caseload of mainstream schools and will allocate visits across the school year. These visits are primarily to focus on pupils who will struggle to access a mainstream curriculum without a high level of personalised adaptive learning. Pupils due to transition to a new setting and those at risk of exclusion are also prioritised.
Other support is available, for example: training; modelling; parent support and supporting pupils who may need less help academically but need other support relating to their autism, e.g. emotional regulation. This support should be short-term and focussed with clear goals and an end date.
We support children regardless of whether or not they have an EHCP. For pupils who require support with curriculum planning, we expect schools to apply for an EHCP.
Where there is a query or crisis concerning a particular student, SENDCos should phone or email to discuss the student before inviting the outreach teacher in to school to observe or meet with staff/parents. Outreach teachers may be able to suggest strategies without school staff needing to wait for an available school visit.
Outreach teachers expect school staff to take minutes and write notes during conversations. Written feedback will be provided when appropriate, however, we are unable to provide written feedback for each student for every visit.
PRE-DIAGNOSIS SUPPORT
Pupils who are awaiting an autism diagnosis may be referred for a short-term piece of work in cases where a referral for an autism assessment has been made to NDT (neurodevelopmental team) or CAMHS (Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services) and parental permission is given. This includes an observation and a TAC (Team Around a Child Meeting) and the primary focus will be on setting up routines and supporting families.
ANNUAL REVIEWS AND 8 WEEK PLANNING MEETINGS
When an autistic pupil receives an EHCP, a member of the outreach service may attend an TAC meeting about the pupil and provide advice and support on how best to meet their needs and the type of support they will receive in future.
Outreach teachers will attend annual reviews for pupils in years 5 and 6 or those considering change of placement. Any other annual reviews attended are at the discretion of the outreach teacher and should only be done where it is felt that this is the best use of time.
SECONDARY SCHOOL SUPPORT
The main focus in secondary schools will be on whole school support and modelling. POS will help introduce and implement a plan of interventions covering topics such as revision and puberty. POS will also support with capturing pupil voice and transition to adulthood.

Parents
Parent workshops
Phoenix Outreach Service run a termly course for families called LEAF (Linking and Empowering Autistic Families). This is a seven week course which offers an introduction to autism, covering topics such as Communication and Emotional Regulation. We also offer other workshops throughout the year, including evening workshops to enable working parents to attend. Any parents living in Tower Hamlets or whose children attend a school, college or nursery in setting Tower Hamlets are able to attend, regardless of whether the setting is supported by POS.
In addition, schools can request coffee mornings or parent workshops from their outreach teacher. If parents of autistic children would like POS support in school, they should first discuss with their school SENCo.
To book on to parent courses or for more information, please contact training@phoenix.towerhamlets.sch.uk
This website is updated termly with lists of workshops for that term. Parents can also request to be on our mailing list to hear of courses every term.

Our Sites
Our Phoenix Primary site at Bow Road, is our provision for all Primary-aged pupils. This site has 23 classes, and specialist facilities such as a soft play room, sensory room, OT spaces, and water therapy.
​Our Phoenix Secondary site at Paton Close, is our provision for all Secondary and Sixth Form-aged pupils. This site has 21 classes, and specialist facilities such as a multi sensory room, OT spaces, and state of the art MUGA.​
In the Primary Satellite pupils follow a broad curriculum based around the National Curriculum for core subjects; Literacy, Maths, Science, Computing, and PSHE and the International Primary Curriculum (IPC) for other foundation subjects. The IPC is a comprehensive, thematic, creative curriculum followed by our partner school which is modified for the needs of our pupils. The curriculum is designed in such a way to maximise social interaction and inclusion opportunities where appropriate with mainstream pupils. Specific learning goals for every subject are set with a focus on international mindedness and reflection on personal learning.
Please click on the above image to visit Marner school website.
The Phoenix Satellite at Bow School currently has three classes made up of students between the ages of 11 and 16. Many of the students have come from Phoenix while others have come into the Satellite from mainstream Primary schools in the local area.
Students are identified for the Satellite programme considering their academic abilities, emotional regulation and socialisation skills. Learning in this setting provides opportunities for inclusion and preparation for the next stage of their education. Each class follows the Phoenix School curriculum with a focus on extending and challenging students in all areas of their curriculum.
